record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: (A. Glutsyuk, S. Tabachnikov [210]) Given two nested closed convex hypersurfaces, assume that the billiard transformations on the set of orien ted lines that intersect both hypersurfaces commute. Prove that the hypersurfaces are confocal ellipso ids. The above problem also has analogs in the elliptic and hyperbolic geomet ries. Namely, one can define quadrics in the elliptic and hyperbolic geometries: a quadratic hypers urface of the unit sphere is, by definition, its intersection with a quadratic cone, and a similar definitio n applies to the hyperboloid model of the hyperbolic geometry. It is known that the billiard maps in quadrics are completely integrable in the geometries of constant curvature, see, e.g., [206 ]. 4.3 Generalized pentagram maps We already mentioned the pentagram map. This map sends a (generic ) polygon in the projective plane to a new polygon whose vertices are the intersection points of the consecutive short diagonals of the original polygon. The map extends to twisted n-gons, bi-infinite collections of point ( vi) satisfying vi+n = M (vi) for all i, where M is a projective transformation. The pentagram map also commutes with projective transformations (since it only involves points and line s, and the operations of connecting pairs of points by lines and intersecting lines), hence the pentagram map is defined on the moduli space of projective equivalence classes of polygons. Numerous generalizations of the pentagram map were introduced a nd studied, in particular, in [131, 132, 133, 156]. Following [132], we describe one class of such generaliz ed pentagram maps and present some problems and conjectures. Let ( vi) be a twisted polygon in RPd. Fix two ( d - 1)-tuples of integers I = (i1,..., id- 1), J = (j1,..., jd- 1). Define the hyperplanes Pk = Span(vk, vk+i1, vk+i1+i2,..., vk+i1+...+id-1 ), and consider the new point TI,J (vk) = Pk ∩ Pk+j1 ∩ Pk+j1+j2 ∩... ∩ Pk+j1+...+jd-1. 18 This formula defines the generalized pentagram map TI,J. In this notation, the usual pentagram map is T(2),(1). For some of these maps, for example, T(2,2),(1,1), T(2,1),(1,1), and T(3,1),(1,1), complete integrability has been established [131, 133, 156]. Other cases were studied numeric ally in [132]. This study was based on the height criterion [110, 95]. The height of a rational number p/q, given in the lowest terms, is max( |p|, |q|). In appropriate coordinates, TI,J is a rational map defined over Q. One considers the growth of the maximal heights of the coordinat es under iterations of the map. For integrable maps, one expects a slower growth, and for non-int egrable ones - a faster one. More specifically, a linear growth of the double logarithm of this height is a nu merical indication of non- integrability. In particular, these experiments suggested that the maps T(2,2),(1,2), T(1,2),(1,2), T(1,3),(1,3), T(2,3),(2,3), are integrable, whereas the maps T(1,2),(3,1), T(1,2),(1,3), T(2,3),(1,1), T(2,4),(1,1), T(3,3),(1,1) are not integrable.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ be two nested closed convex hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d\ge 2$) with smooth strictly convex boundaries, with $\Sigma_1$ enclosed by $\Sigma_2$. Each hypersurface $\Sigma_i$ induces a billiard reflection map $B_i$ acting on the space of oriented lines in $\mathbb{R}^d$: a line $\ell$ that meets $\Sigma_i$ transversally is sent to its reflection at the first intersection point with $\Sigma_i$, with the angle of incidence equal to the angle of reflection. Consider the common domain consisting of oriented lines that intersect both $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$. Assume that the billiard maps $B_1$ and $B_2$ commute on this common domain, i.e.\ $B_1\circ B_2 = B_2\circ B_1$ wherever both sides are defined. Prove that $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ are confocal ellipsoids (i.e.\ ellipsoids belonging to a common confocal family). Establish the corresponding statement for nested closed convex hypersurfaces in the elliptic and hyperbolic geometries of constant curvature, where a quadric in elliptic geometry is the intersection of the unit sphere with a quadratic cone, and a quadric in hyperbolic geometry is defined analogously using the hyperboloid model.
artifact.status_search_result: Glutsyuk has proven the Commuting Billiards Conjecture in full: the two-dimensional case in earlier work and the higher-dimensional case (including the constant curvature versions in elliptic and hyperbolic geometries) in his 2018 preprint "On commuting billiards in higher-dimensional spaces of constant curvature" (arXiv:1807.10567). The proof uses an extension of Berger's theorem on caustics of higher-dimensional billiards.

status_evidence.title: On commuting billiards in higher-dimensional spaces of constant curvature
status_evidence.snippet: If the corresponding actions by reflections on the space of oriented lines commute, then the billiards are confocal ellipsoids... together solve completely the Commuting Billiard Conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Glutsyuk proved the commuting billiards conjecture in all dimensions and in spaces of constant curvature.
